Working notes:

- Performance is reported only in rolling aggregate windows, not by day or angle. Results improved from 2/5 to 3/5 landed, but attribution is impossible.
- Do not infer that B or D caused the reported results; continue testing consistently if measurement matters.
- Prefer quality (B) or testimonial (D) as lower-pressure, evergreen options when no experiment is required. Avoid assuming discounts or urgency are superior.
- Two unsubscribes were reported through support on some days, but there is insufficient evidence linking them to any angle.
- No deliverability complaints were reported on relevant days.

Working notes:

- B has been used repeatedly through Day 20; D was used once. A and C remain untested or minimally tested.
- Results are available only as rolling aggregate windows, not by day or angle. Aggregate performance improved from 2/5 to 3/5, then reached 4/5; no causal attribution is possible.
- Do not infer that repeated B use caused the 4/5 result. If measurement matters, rotate angles deliberately and keep other conditions consistent.
- B and D remain suitable lower-pressure, evergreen defaults when no experiment is required. There is no evidence that price cuts or urgency perform better.
- Two unsubscribes were reported through support on some days, but they cannot be linked to any angle.
- No deliverability complaints have been reported, including Days 11–20.
- Banner refreshes, modest list growth, and legal sign-offs occurred, but none establish angle-level impact.

Working notes:

- B was used repeatedly through Day 20; D was used once earlier and again on Days 26 and 28; A was tested repeatedly on Days 21–25, 27, and 30; C was tested on Day 29. A and C are no longer untested, but exposure remains too limited for reliable comparison.

- Do not infer that any angle caused an aggregate result. A’s repeated appearances alongside 1/5 windows do not establish that A underperformed, because window composition and other conditions are unknown.

- Two unsubscribes were reported through support; they cannot be linked to any angle.
- No deliverability complaints have been reported through Day 30.

Working notes:

- Since Day 30, C was used most often, with B once and D twice; A was not used. Do not treat this as a valid comparison because results are pooled and angle exposure is unbalanced.
- The only new aggregate result was 3/5 for the last five pushes (through Day 40), following earlier 1/5 windows. No per-day or per-angle breakdown exists, so no angle—especially C—can be credited or blamed.

Working notes:
